A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PCI research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. All scientific material can be matched; v2 adds an acknowledgment page.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-insertion experiments across five generative models, quantitative editing comparisons in Table 1, and empirical ablations and extended analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original multi-model concept-insertion results, editing comparisons, and appendix experiments reported in v1.

M1.justification: PCI prompt switching, concept-controlled seed filtering and negative guidance, VQA-based CIS scoring, and CIS-guided editing remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same approximately 800 concept descriptions and 88 editing prompt pairs. Coverage of concept deletion, context variation, multiple concepts, and abstract concepts is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure D7 retain NTI+P2P and Stable Flow as editing comparators. Appendix C.1 also retains the same four VQA models; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The inference configurations, timestep normalization, CIS crossing thresholds, and three CLIP editing metrics are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix B. No experimental protocol or setting is revised.

E4.justification: The VQA-model, seed-budget, and prompt-variation ablations in Appendix C are identical. Concept deletion, fine-grained context analyses, attention visualizations, multi-concept interactions, and abstract-concept analyses are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the 100-seed CIS setup, 20 seeds per editing pair, bootstrap seed-budget analysis, 95% Wilson confidence intervals, and means and standard deviations across concept–prompt pairs.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains every numerical result; for example, PCI at tau60 still reports CLIPimg/CLIPtxt/CLIPdir of 0.8625/0.2289/0.1531. The main-text and appendix plots, qualitative examples, and reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The PCI equations, diffusion preliminaries, CIS/CDS formulations, crossing-time definitions, and multi-concept formulation remain identical in Section 3 and Appendices A, B, and D. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free temporal probing, context- and model-dependent concept dynamics, and CIS-guided editing. The publication-status update does not change these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of context alignment, model differences, deletion dynamics, and concept interactions are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same runtime and editing-sensitivity limitations.

D1.justification: The abstract's 'PCI Framework' hyperlink changes from a direct GitHub repository link to the PCI project website. Implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the new destination changes code availability or resources.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the positioning relative to prior interpretability and editing methods are unchanged. The new funding acknowledgments introduce no related research.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the preprint header with ICLR 2026 publication information, updates version metadata, adds imec to an affiliation, and appends funding acknowledgments. Scientific prose and section ordering remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The running header changes, spacing on the appendix contents page is slightly tightened, and a separate acknowledgment page is added. Scientific figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the scientific methods, results, explanations, and limitations without substantive revision. Publication and affiliation updates and fuller funding attribution improve administrative completeness, but do not materially change scientific rigor or clarity. The resource-link redirection provides no local evidence of improved reproducibility or access.
